name: Waveshare UGV Rover
description: A 6-wheel, rocker-arm-suspension AI robotics kit from Waveshare, built around a Raspberry Pi 4B/5 (or optional Jetson Orin) with an ESP32 motor sub-controller and an optional 2-axis pan-tilt camera module. It's a distinct, higher-tier sibling to the bare Waveshare UGV02 chassis already in this catalog — and, like TurtleBot4 in this same subcategory, Waveshare markets it purely as an educational AI-development platform, not a security product.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: with pan-tilt module; 1.87kg without, per Waveshare's official spec table

specs.label: Connectivity
specs.note: browser-based control, no app install needed

specs.label: Compute
specs.note: + ESP32 sub-controller; Jetson Orin Nano/NX kit also sold

specs.label: Camera
specs.note: optional 2-axis pan-tilt add-on; no IR/night-vision sensor

specs.label: Software
specs.note: Debian Bookworm; GitHub firmware licensed GPL-3.0

specs.label: Speed
specs.note: trades the tracked UGV Beast's off-road grip for speed

specs.label: Subscription
specs.note: local WebRTC browser control, open-source firmware — no cloud account required

sourcing: Verified against Waveshare's own product pages and wiki for the UGV Rover, UGV Rover ROS2 Kit, UGV Beast, UGV01, UGV02, WAVE ROVER, and RaspRover; the shared `waveshareteam/ugv_rpi` GitHub repository; independent coverage from CNX-Software and Hackster.io; and distributor listings (RobotShop, Core Electronics, eBay). Flagged as uncertain or corrected: this catalog's prior generic name ("Waveshare UGV Rover Series") has been narrowed to the specific model shown in this photo — a 6-wheel UGV Rover, not the tracked UGV Beast or the bare UGV02 chassis already catalogued separately; the "Security" framing itself, which no official Waveshare source supports and which this catalog keeps only as a maker-adaptation caveat, matching the same concern already raised on TurtleBot4; and current AliExpress pricing/availability, which could not be independently confirmed at research time.

pricing.summary: Waveshare's own listings range from $244.99 for the bare chassis kit up to $486.99 for the full PT/ROS2 configuration with the Raspberry Pi and pan-tilt camera module included; a Jetson Orin Nano/NX compute variant runs higher still. It's sold directly through waveshare.com and through general electronics/robotics distributors including RobotShop, Core Electronics, and eBay — no AliExpress storefront listing was confirmed at research time, though Waveshare typically maintains one.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Firmware for this lineup is genuinely open-source (GPL-3.0), though the hardware design files carry no formal open-hardware license. Its turret light is a visible-spectrum LED spotlight, not an IR/night-vision sensor, despite how it may look in photos.
